anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 mine has one 5x5x3 isometric scene, four directly exposed targets, one lava and one support hazard, and no sealed targets. The visible control problem is camera rotation plus exposed face clicking; a failed strike changes durability or collapses the support. Two-Lamp Dyeworks has fewer spatial hazards but adds a discrete spectral recipe, irreversible dosing, two-lamp comparison, and full plunger/stir/strip control. It is therefore materially above this low-end spatial anchor on decision coupling, while not necessarily harder on spatial aiming.

evidence.explanation: The approved L1 configuration is four targets with one screen, one lava block, one support block, durability margin two, and unsealed targets.
The generator constructs blockers, optional screens, lava/support hazards, ray-solvable extraction steps, and explicitly unsealed or sealed prerequisites.
The browser records rotations and canvas raycast mines; target sealing, lava, support collapse, durability, and inventory visibly alter the board.
The independent grader replays camera orientation, click-ray occlusion, removals, hazards, durability, resets, and extracted inventory.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 constellation is an active-search field with 112 target stars, noise, two false convergence points, a 112-pixel reveal radius, and a 28-pixel accepted click at baseline. The cursor reveals the shape, but the only state-changing decision is where to make the final selection. Dyeworks requires selecting a recipe, accumulating irreversible units, re-sampling after state changes, and proving the same current strip under both lamps, so even its easiest profile retains more dependent state than this L2 one-shot search.

evidence.explanation: The approved L2 baseline exposes two decoys, 26 noise stars, a 112-pixel reveal radius, and a 28-pixel accepted radius.
The approved generator creates the moving cursor field, target shape, decoys, noise, reveal parameters, and expected click.
The visible UI either moves a mouse over the canvas and clicks once or uses coordinate controls and then selects the current point.
The grader checks the submitted click/input surface against the expected point; it does not replay a dependent multi-action world.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 board has three ordered lamps, three walls, three wells, momentum physics, a 50 ms tick, and a minimum of 72 ticks and eight control changes. Its key burden is continuous spatial steering and recovery from live collisions. Dyeworks has no moving physical state on the clean path, but its discrete spectral recipe, irreversible composition, two-illuminant tolerance, and full direct-manipulation witnesses create a different planning and precision burden. This supports Dyeworks d2/d3 being below or around the L3 anchor rather than treating every longer sequence as harder.

evidence.explanation: The approved L3 profile specifies three lamps, three walls, three hazards, 50 ms physics, and minimum tick/control-change requirements.
The generator makes the ordered gates, walls, hazards, physics constants, and minimum requirements active in the generated state.
The browser advances position and velocity on every physics tick, handles wall bounces and well resets, and activates lamps in order.
The grader deterministically replays each tick and requires the ordered lamps, minimum ticks, minimum controls, and final cup.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 courier uses an 18x11 warehouse, five barriers, five ordered face gates, four sparse scanners, and a 48–105-roll route while the die orientation is hidden between scanners. Dyeworks d4 has a shorter clean path and no hidden orientation memory, but adds a four-pigment irreversible recipe, active-dye and unit bounds, two-lamp spectral ambiguity, three-vat recovery, and three full gesture witnesses. These are comparable L4 burdens in different dimensions; Dyeworks is not supported as higher than L4 merely because its recipe uses more numeric fields.

evidence.explanation: The approved L4 configuration is the 18x11, five-gate, four-scanner, 48–105-roll initial-and-scanner orientation condition with full keyboard control.
The generator builds the barrier maze, orientation-constrained gates, sparse scanners, and bounded route.
The UI hides orientation away from scanners and checks top/east face requirements at gates.
The grader replays every roll, orientation transition, wall/gate decision, scanner condition, route, and ordered gate crossing.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 candy task requires four valid adjacent swaps whose accepted swaps change the 5x5 board, trigger deterministic gravity/refill and multi-wave scoring, avoid terminal black licorice, and hit an exact score. Dyeworks d5 narrows its color tolerance and recovery but can still solve with one successful composition chain followed by one stir, one dip, two lamp views, and certification; it does not expose the same changing-board route planning. Dyeworks d5 is therefore a high end of its own ladder but is not source-supported as an absolute L5 match.

evidence.explanation: The approved L5 profile requires four changing-board swaps, at least seven cascade waves, a five-cell preview, and a forbidden candy.
The generator enumerates routes over changed boards and selects exact-score multi-wave instances subject to the profile.
The visible match engine removes matches, consumes the refill stream, collapses columns, and makes the next board state depend on the accepted swap.
The grader replays swaps and cascades and requires exact score, move budget, minimum wave, and untouched licorice.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only agent reads the visible lot rule (3–4 active dye families, 8–11 total units, and ΔE 4.2), the four labelled pigment bottles, the pinned ribbon, the current lamp, the wet-proof strip, the composition ledger, vat headroom, fresh-vat count, and the two-lamp proof ledger. It must choose integer doses without exceeding the irreversible vat, use the full syringe plunger for each dose, stir the vat through a complete circular gesture, drag the fresh strip into the visible vat opening, compare the sample against the ribbon under north-light, toggle to sodium, and verify the same current strip again. A dose invalidates the previous sample; an incorrect mix can only be abandoned with DUMP THIS VAT, consuming one of three vats. Success requires a current sample whose composition is unchanged, both lamps viewed, the visible lot bounds satisfied, both spectral ΔE values within tolerance, and certification. The exact event sequence, dose totals, lamp views, and full gesture witnesses are replayed by the grader.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The implemented d4/full configuration is a defensible L4 placement. It is clearly more dependent than the L2 Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt because additions permanently change the mixture and every certification attempt depends on a newly sampled current composition. It is below the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade on changing-state planning, because a successful dye run does not change the decision surface after each accepted action. It is comparable to the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier: Dyeworks trades the courier's long route and hidden orientation memory for spectral recipe selection, cross-illuminant matching, recovery, and three precise direct-manipulation witnesses. The L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board is harder on continuous live momentum and collision recovery, but that does not make this static spectral task automatically below L4. The source supports keeping the assigned label while treating the absolute placement as provisional pending calibration.

evidence.explanation: The assigned baseline is d4/full and its active d4 parameters are four pigments, 3–4 active dyes, 8–11 units, three vats, ΔE 4.2, and a generated two-lamp near-metamer condition.
Target selection searches integer recipes under the visible lot rule and, at d4, retains targets with a daylight-close, sodium-different alternative.
The browser resets sampling after every dose and only considers a recipe ready after current composition, lot bounds, both lamp views, and both ΔE checks pass.
Full interaction requires sampled stir and strip gestures, while lamp toggling records the second view of the unchanged sample.
The independent grader binds the transcript to the task and interaction, replays all state changes and gestures, and checks both illuminants and final certification.

uncertainties: No human or screenshot-only agent calibration was run, so the L4 placement is a source-based judgment rather than a measured percentile.
The source does not establish how consistently target colors can be distinguished across displays or seeds.
The generated near-metamer is a target-selection condition; the source does not expose a separate visible decoy recipe.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose from two bottles, set an integer dose with minus/plus controls, inject irreversibly, press STIR VAT and DIP STRIP, flip the lamp, and certify a 1–2-dye, 2–3-unit mixture.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 1–2 active dyes and 2–3 units, match the target within ΔE 7.0 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before the fifth-vat limit is exhausted.
profiles.rationale: This is the easiest source-supported profile of the mechanic, but not automatically L1: it still combines spectral visual comparison, an irreversible dose state, two lamp views, and a stir/dip chain. It is below d4 and is closer to the low end around the L2 constellation search than to the changing-state L3/L5 references. The simplified controls reduce motor execution burden without changing the recipe problem.

evidence.explanation: The d1 profile has two pigments, 1–2 active components, 2–3 total units, five fresh vats, and ΔE 7.0.
The browser applies the active-component and total-unit bounds to the visible recipe.
Simplified mode binds dose, stir, dip, lamp, certify, and dump to explicit visible controls.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose from two bottles, drag the syringe to integer graduations, inject irreversibly, stir with a complete circular vat gesture, drag the strip into the vat, flip the lamp, and certify a 1–2-dye, 2–3-unit mixture.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 1–2 active dyes and 2–3 units, match the target within ΔE 7.0 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before the fifth-vat limit is exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The world and spectral decision are the same as d1/simplified; full mode adds direct-manipulation precision for the plunger, circular stir, and strip drop. The source supports the same low-end task placement with a higher motor-control burden, not a new recipe or state dependency.

evidence.explanation: The d1 parameters are independent of interaction mode.

Full stirring and strip dipping require visible gesture geometry before producing the same stir/dip state transitions.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose among three bottles, make a 2–3-dye, 4–6-unit integer recipe with dose buttons, then perform the explicit stir/dip, two-lamp inspection, and certification loop.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 2–3 active dyes and 4–6 units, match within ΔE 6.0 under daylight and sodium, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before four vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The third pigment and higher lot bounds create more coupled recipe choices than d1, while every accepted dose still invalidates the sample and cannot be removed. Four recovery vats and a broad tolerance keep this below d4. It is above the L2 one-shot constellation problem but its absence of live momentum makes an exact absolute L3 assignment uncertain; 3 is a provisional source-relative placement.

evidence.explanation: The d2 profile increases the rack to three pigments, requires 2–3 active dyes and 4–6 units, and narrows tolerance to 6.0.
Target recipes are selected using component and total-unit bounds, so these changes alter the valid decision set rather than merely repeating actions.
The replay accumulates irreversible doses and rejects a sample unless the interaction-specific stir and dip sequence is valid.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose among three bottles, drag the syringe to integer graduations for a 2–3-dye, 4–6-unit recipe, perform the full stir and strip gestures, inspect both lamps, and certify.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 2–3 active dyes and 4–6 units, match within ΔE 6.0 under daylight and sodium, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before four vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The full interaction adds the source-checked motor witnesses but preserves d2's valid recipe space and spectral goal. The relative placement remains above d1 and below d4; it is not promoted solely because the gesture transcript is longer.

evidence.explanation: The d2 difficulty parameters are shared across the two interaction modes.
Full and simplified source requirements differ only in expected dose/stir/dip inputs and, for full, gesture validation; the replayed recipe state is shared.

profiles.visible_problem: Use all three bottles and 6–8 total button-selected units, then explicitly stir and dip, compare under both lamps, and certify.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use all three active dyes and 6–8 units, match within ΔE 5.0 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before four vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: This is a real increase over d2 because the active-dye count is forced to exactly three, the total range is higher, and the color tolerance is narrower. The major graduation is mainly a visual marking change, while simplified dose buttons still expose every integer; therefore the ordering is supported mostly by the recipe constraints, not by an assumed loss of dose values. Compared with Gyroscopic Tilt Board L3, the task has stronger discrete mixture reasoning but no continuous live physics.

evidence.explanation: The d3 profile requires exactly three active dyes, 6–8 units, ΔE 5.0, and major graduation support.
The exact-three and 6–8-unit lot constraints are active in the browser readiness calculation.
The independent replay rejects compositions outside the active-component and total-unit bounds.

profiles.visible_problem: Use all three bottles and drag the syringe to 6–8 total units, then complete the circular stir and strip-drop gestures, compare both lamps, and certify.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use all three active dyes and 6–8 units, match within ΔE 5.0 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before four vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The same d3 recipe and spectral constraints apply as in simplified mode. Full mode adds motor precision, but no new world state, target information, or success rule; it remains a provisional L3-scale profile rather than an automatic L4 from gesture counts.

evidence.explanation: The renderer keeps the same visible target, lot book, lamps, vat, and success controls while selecting the full gesture surface.
Full gesture witnesses are checked before the same recipe and two-illuminant certification replay.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose 3–4 of four bottles and 8–11 integer units with dose buttons, then use explicit stir and dip, compare one current strip under north-light and sodium, and seal.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 3–4 active dyes and 8–11 units, match within ΔE 4.2 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before three vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The fourth pigment, broader active-component choice, higher unit range, narrower tolerance, and generated lot-compliant cross-lamp alternative produce the assigned hard recipe problem. Simplified mode removes the three direct gesture witnesses but keeps the same irreversible spectral decisions and proof requirement. This is source-supported as a comparable L4-scale configuration with Blind Dice Courier, not as a claim that its route/memory burden is identical.

evidence.explanation: The d4 profile exposes four pigments, 3–4 active dyes, 8–11 units, three vats, ΔE 4.2, and two-lamp metamer selection.
The d4 metamer parameters change which target recipes are eligible by requiring a daylight-close, sodium-different alternative.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose 3–4 of four bottles, drag the syringe to integer graduations for 8–11 units, circularly stir, drag the strip into the vat, compare both lamps, and seal.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 3–4 active dyes and 8–11 units, match within ΔE 4.2 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before three vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: This is the current baseline. Full mode adds plunger endpoint, sampled circular sweep, and inner-ellipse strip-drop precision to the d4 recipe and two-lamp problem. It is above the simplified input burden but preserves the same world, information, goal, and graded action effects.

evidence.explanation: The baseline is d4/full and the full surface is explicitly the plunger, circular stir, and strip drag.
The full stir and dip handlers require sampled movement, distance, sweep, and visible vat geometry.
The grader independently validates plunger, stir, and strip gesture witnesses, including the inner ellipse.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose 3–4 of four bottles and 10–12 button-selected units, resolve the tighter two-lamp match, use explicit stir and dip, and preserve the last of two vats.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 3–4 active dyes and 10–12 units, match within ΔE 3.6 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before two vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: D5 is visibly and mechanically tighter than d4: the total range and daylight tolerance narrow, the sparse marks reduce dose labeling, and only two recovery vats remain. Its clean successful path still has the same single composition-to-sample-to-two-lamp proof chain and button actions, so the approved L5 Candy reference is materially more state-dependent. I therefore treat d5 as a high L4-scale profile in absolute terms while preserving its source-supported ordering above d4.

evidence.explanation: The d5 profile narrows the lot to 10–12 units and ΔE 3.6, uses sparse graduations, and leaves two vats.
Sparse support only changes which graduation marks and labels are rendered, while the vat bank is rendered from fresh_vats.
The d5 success replay remains the same two-illuminant certification and final composition check, with dumps only affecting recovery/exhaustion.

profiles.visible_problem: Choose 3–4 of four bottles, drag the sparse syringe to 10–12 units, complete the full stir and strip gestures, compare both lamps, and preserve the last of two vats.
profiles.success_condition: A current sampled composition must use 3–4 active dyes and 10–12 units, match within ΔE 3.6 under both lamps, be viewed under both lamps, and be certified before two vats are exhausted.
profiles.rationale: The full d5 profile combines the tighter d5 recipe and recovery constraints with the same three source-checked direct gestures as d4. It is ordered above d4 within this mechanic, but the lack of additional changing-state decisions keeps an absolute L5 assignment unsupported by the approved Candy reference.

evidence.explanation: The d5 parameters and full interaction surface are explicit in the controls.
The full renderer preserves the same d5 target, lamp, vat, proof, and certification structure while exposing physical controls.
The full interaction changes the required input witnesses but not the replayed d5 success condition.

mode_changes.simplified: The visible rack grows from two to three pigments; the lot changes from 1–2 active dyes and 2–3 units to 2–3 active dyes and 4–6 units; tolerance narrows from 7.0 to 6.0 and recovery drops from five to four vats. Dose, stir, and dip remain explicit controls.
mode_changes.full: The same recipe-space and recovery changes apply, while plunger, circular-stir, and strip-drag witnesses remain the input surface.

adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The pair is meaningfully ordered because the valid recipe set and visible rack change, not because there are more independent actions. A third pigment and a higher active/total requirement create more coupled dose choices; the lack of a metamer constraint and the extra recovery vat keep d2 below d4.

evidence.explanation: The d1-to-d2 parameter changes are explicit in the two profiles.
Pigment count, component bounds, total bounds, and capacity are used when enumerating valid target recipes.
Dose additions are irreversible and reset the sample, so the changed recipe bounds affect later decisions.

mode_changes.simplified: The same three-bottle rack now requires all three active dyes, 6–8 rather than 4–6 units, and ΔE 5.0 rather than 6.0; major rather than numbered marks are shown. Dose buttons, explicit stir, and explicit dip remain.
mode_changes.full: The same recipe and tolerance changes apply; full plunger control displays major marks, but the plunger still selects integer units.

adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The exact-three constraint and narrower color tolerance change the decision problem. The graduation change is only a perceptual marking change: the simplified buttons still step integers and the full handler rounds to integers. The pair is therefore distinguished, but its ordering is supported by recipe feasibility and tolerance more strongly than by syringe precision.

evidence.explanation: The d2 and d3 profiles show the exact-three, total-range, tolerance, and graduation changes.
Graduation support changes tick visibility and labels only.
The component and total-unit constraints are checked as actual success conditions.

mode_changes.simplified: The rack grows from three to four pigments; the lot changes from exactly 3 active dyes and 6–8 units to 3–4 active dyes and 8–11 units; tolerance narrows to 4.2, fresh vats drop to three, and a daylight-close/sodium-different target-selection condition is added. The explicit button surface stays the same.
mode_changes.full: The same recipe and target-distribution changes apply, while graduation display returns from major to numbered and the full gesture witnesses stay the same.

adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The pair is net harder because the extra pigment and metamer-constrained target distribution increase spectral ambiguity and the tolerance narrows. Numbered rather than major marks improve dose legibility, so that one presentation change reverses locally; it does not erase the larger recipe and two-light increase. The metamer condition is an indirect generator constraint rather than a separately visible decoy.

evidence.explanation: The d3-to-d4 changes include the fourth pigment, wider active range, higher totals, lower tolerance, fewer vats, and metamer thresholds.
Metamer thresholds alter target eligibility by comparing daylight and sodium ΔE for alternate recipes.
The return to numbered graduations is a visible information improvement, which is a local reversal within an otherwise harder profile.

mode_changes.simplified: The four-bottle rack remains, but the lot tightens from 8–11 to 10–12 units and ΔE 4.2 to 3.6, daylight metamer threshold also narrows, marks become sparse, and fresh vats drop from three to two. Button controls and the two-lamp proof loop remain.
mode_changes.full: The same tighter recipe, sparse-mark, and recovery changes apply to the same plunger, circular-stir, and strip-drag surface.

adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The pair is meaningfully but modestly ordered: the tolerance and allowed total range narrow, sparse marks reduce visible dose guidance, and a wrong trial has less recovery. Capacity remains above every profile's valid target maximum, and a clean successful run still needs only one composition chain, so this is a high-end refinement rather than a new changing-state stage. The source supports d5 above d4 within this mechanic, not an absolute L5 equivalence to Exact-Change Candy Cascade.

evidence.explanation: The d4-to-d5 changes are explicit in the two parameter objects.
Sparse marks change visible guidance and fresh_vats changes the visible recovery bank.
Vat count affects only dump-and-restart recovery; a successful first-vat run does not consume the additional vats.

current_default_equivalence.claim: The uncontrolled task defaults to the same d4 parameter values as the explicit d4 baseline, and the interaction defaults to full. For a fixed seed, the generator's rack and target selection use the mechanic, difficulty, and seed rather than interaction, so the physical challenge and full action semantics are intended to match.
current_default_equivalence.qualification: This is not byte-for-byte identity: materialized controlled tasks receive a new task id/name/version and add control_condition metadata, so challenge_id and exported identity differ even when the generated rack, target, parameters, and full action effects match.

evidence.explanation: The current uncontrolled task has the hard d4 natural-language task and full mouse/keyboard environment.
Without a control condition the generator supplies d4 defaults; its target-selection RNG uses seed, mechanic, and difficulty, while task id only enters challenge identity.
Controlled materialization changes task metadata and attaches difficulty/interaction parameters and live clock metadata.
The controlled task directory and copied hooks receive an interaction- and difficulty-specific task id.

missing_evidence: No pre-controls implementation snapshot, generated artifact, or historical source record was supplied, so preservation against the actual historical implementation cannot be established.
No multi-seed generation or browser/grader comparison was run in this audit.

findings.claim: vat_capacity_units and fresh_vats are active safeguards and recovery affordances, but they are weak primary separators for the clean solution path.
findings.causal_explanation: Every profile's valid target_total_max is below its vat_capacity_units, so capacity does not constrain a valid canonical recipe. fresh_vats is consulted when the agent dumps a failed vat; a correct first-vat run never uses the extra vats. These parameters can affect recovery after a wrong irreversible attempt, but their numeric changes do not independently deepen the successful decision problem.

evidence.explanation: Across d1–d5, capacity is 6, 8, 10, 13, 13 while target maxima are 3, 6, 8, 11, 12; fresh-vat counts are the recovery values 5, 4, 4, 3, 2.
Target candidates are bounded by target totals and only additionally filtered by the larger vat capacity during recipe enumeration.
Capacity rejects an over-dose and fresh-vat count is used for recovery, while dose composition and sampling are the actual clean-path state changes.
DUMP THIS VAT clears the mixture and advances the vat only after an agent chooses recovery.

findings.recommended_action: Retain these parameters as visible guardrails, but do not use their magnitudes as the main justification for adjacent-level difficulty. Use multi-seed failure/recovery data before treating them as an independent ladder driver.

findings.claim: graduation_support changes visible marking, not the available integer dose action space.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser hides or labels tick marks according to graduation_support, but full mode still rounds the plunger ratio to any integer from 1 through maximum and simplified mode still changes the dose by one. The grader checks integer units and gesture endpoint consistency, not whether the selected graduation was numbered, major, or sparse. The parameter can add screenshot ambiguity, but it is not a finer motor-control or dose-resolution rule.

evidence.explanation: The profiles change graduation_support from major to numbered to sparse.
graduation_support only controls hidden/faint marks and labels in tickMarkup.
Simplified mode changes dose in one-unit increments regardless of graduation_support.
Full mode rounds the continuous plunger position to an integer dose and records the endpoint.
The full grader validates dose units and endpoint ratios, with no graduation-support contract.

findings.recommended_action: Count graduation support as a visible-information change only; do not describe major or sparse marks as reduced dose precision without an additional active rule.

findings.claim: The d4/d5 metamer thresholds affect target generation, but do not expose a separate visible decoy or an independently graded metamer choice.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator uses daylight and sodium ΔE thresholds to retain target recipes with a qualifying alternate and stores the selected alternate only in ground_truth.near_metamer. The public UI exposes the two target swatches and the two-lamp rule, while the grader checks the submitted mixture directly under both illuminants and never checks near_metamer. Thus the thresholds can change instance ambiguity, but the visible two-lamp decision is already present in every profile and the hidden alternate is not itself an action.

evidence.explanation: Metamer thresholds filter alternate recipes during target selection.
The public state contains target displays/labs and parameters, while the near_metamer record is added only to ground truth.
The visible renderer shows target and sample swatches under the current lamp, not a decoy recipe.
Certification recomputes the submitted mixture's two illuminant ΔE values; it does not require or inspect near_metamer.

findings.recommended_action: Describe the metamer settings as target-distribution ambiguity rather than as a separate visible subtask; retain the two-lamp comparison itself as the active task rule.

concise_summary: Keep the assigned d4/full baseline. Source evidence supports a relative ladder d1 < d2 < d3 < d4 < d5, with d1 around L2, d2/d3 around L3, and d4/d5 high-L4 rather than treating d5 as an absolute L5 equivalent. The only source-supported concerns are that capacity/fresh-vat values are mainly guardrails or recovery and graduation/metamer settings are weaker or more indirect than their summaries imply.
limitations: This is source analysis only; no browser, generated multi-seed comparison, grader run, exported-verifier run, human calibration, or computer-use evaluation was performed.
The source provides no historical pre-controls implementation snapshot, so historical preservation cannot be established.
The source does not establish screenshot-only success rates or display-dependent perceptual difficulty.
